nodes.summary: For a letter $a$ of $\alpha$, the copy domino of $a$ is the domino over the extended alphabet whose top and bottom are both the one-letter word $a$.
nodes.title: Copy domino

nodes.summary: Let $(R, x, y)$ be a reachability instance and read words over $\alpha$ as words of letters. Let $A$ be a sequence of dominoes of the MPCP instance of $(R, x, y)$. For all words $v, s, t$ over $\alpha$, if $s$ rewrites to $t$ under $R$ in zero or more steps and the top of $A$ equals $v \star t$ followed by the bottom of $A$, where $\star$ is the row separator, then $s v$ rewrites to $y$ under $R$ in zero or more…
nodes.title: The backward direction of the MPCP reduction

nodes.summary: For a list of rules $R$, a word $x$ derives a word $y$ when $x$ rewrites to $y$ in zero or more steps of $R$, that is, when $(x, y)$ lies in the reflexive-transitive closure of the one-step rewriting relation of $R$.
nodes.title: Derivations in a string rewriting system

nodes.summary: Let $(R, x, y)$ be a reachability instance and read words over $\alpha$ as words of letters. If a word $w$ over $\alpha$ rewrites to $y$ under $R$ in zero or more steps and every letter of $w$ occurs in a rule of $R$, in $x$ or in $y$, then there is a sequence $A$ of dominoes of the MPCP instance of $(R, x, y)$ whose top is $w \star$ followed by the bottom of $A$, where $\star$ is the row separator.
nodes.title: The forward direction of the MPCP reduction

nodes.summary: Let $u, v$ be words over $\alpha$, read as words of letters, and let $X, Y$ be words over the extended alphabet of $\alpha$. If $u X = v \star Y$, where $\star$ is the row separator, then there is a word $w$ over $\alpha$ with $v = u w$ and $X = w \star Y$.
nodes.title: Comparing words of letters before a separator

nodes.summary: For a word $y$ over $\alpha$, the final domino of $y$ is the domino over the extended alphabet with top $y \star \diamond$ and bottom $\diamond$, where $y$ is read as a word of letters, $\star$ is the row separator and $\diamond$ is the end marker.
nodes.title: Final domino

nodes.summary: For every letter $a$ of the alphabet $\alpha$, the symbol $a$ of the extended alphabet of the MPCP-to-PCP reduction is different from the star $\star$.
nodes.title: Letters differ from the star

nodes.summary: A word $a_1 \cdots a_n$ over $\alpha$ is sent to the word $a_1 \cdots a_n$ over the extended alphabet of $\alpha$ in which each $a_i$ is read as a letter.
nodes.title: Lifting a word to the extended alphabet

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with a primitive recursive coding, and let $\alpha'$ be $\alpha$ extended with two new symbols, the star and the end marker. There is a computable function $f$ from instances $(R, x, y)$ of the reachability problem over $\alpha$, where $R$ is a list of rewriting rules over $\alpha$ and $x$ and $y$ are words over $\alpha$, to finite lists of dominoes over $\alpha'$ such that, for every…
nodes.title: Reachability with nonempty sides many-one reduces to MPCP with nonempty words

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with a primitive recursive coding, let $\alpha'$ be $\alpha$ extended with two new symbols, the star and the end marker, and let $\alpha''$ be $\alpha'$ extended in the same way by two further new symbols. There is a computable function $f$ from instances $(R, x, y)$ of the reachability problem over $\alpha$, where $R$ is a list of rewriting rules over $\alpha$ and $x$ and $y$ are words…
nodes.title: Reachability for rules with nonempty sides many-one reduces to PCP

nodes.summary: Let $(R, x, y)$ be an instance of the reachability problem over an alphabet $\alpha$. If a word $w$ rewrites to a word $w'$ in one step of $R$ and every letter of $w$ is among the letters of the instance, then every letter of $w'$ is among the letters of the instance.
nodes.title: Rewriting steps keep the letters of the instance

nodes.summary: A string rewriting system $R$, given as a list of rules $(l, r)$, has nonempty sides when every rule of $R$ has a nonempty left side $l$ and a nonempty right side $r$.
nodes.title: Rewriting systems with nonempty sides

nodes.summary: On an instance $(R, x, y)$ of the reachability problem, the reduction returns the MPCP instance of $(R, x, y)$ when every rule of $R$ has a nonempty left side and a nonempty right side, and otherwise the empty list of dominoes, which has no solution.
nodes.title: The total reduction of reachability with nonempty sides to MPCP

nodes.summary: For a rule $(l, r)$ over an alphabet $\alpha$, the domino of the rule has top $l$ and bottom $r$, read as words over the extended alphabet, that is, $\alpha$ together with a star and an end marker.
nodes.title: The domino of a rewriting rule

nodes.summary: A rewriting rule over an alphabet $\alpha$ is a pair $(l, r)$ of words over $\alpha$; applying it replaces an occurrence of $l$ by $r$.
nodes.title: Rewriting rules

nodes.summary: Over the extended alphabet, that is, an alphabet $\alpha$ together with a star $\star$ and an end marker $\diamond$, the separator domino has top and bottom both equal to the one-letter word $\star$; the star separates the rows of a derivation.
nodes.title: The separator domino

nodes.summary: For an instance $(R, x, y)$ of the reachability problem, $x$ rewrites to $y$ in zero or more steps of $R$ if and only if the MPCP instance of $(R, x, y)$ has an MPCP solution, that is, a solution that starts with its first domino.
nodes.title: Reachability reduces to MPCP

nodes.summary: An instance $(R, x, y)$ consists of a string rewriting system $R$, given as a list of rules, and two words $x$ and $y$; it is a yes-instance of the reachability problem when $x$ rewrites to $y$ in zero or more steps of $R$.
nodes.title: The reachability problem for string rewriting

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a word over an alphabet $\alpha$, and extend $\alpha$ by a star $\star$ and an end marker $\diamond$. The start domino of $x$ has top the one-letter word $\diamond$ and bottom the word $\diamond x \star$, with the letters of $x$ read as letters of the extended alphabet.
nodes.title: The start domino of the reduction from reachability to MPCP

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a string rewriting system, given as a list of rules. A word $w$ rewrites to a word $w'$ in one step of $R$ when there are a rule $(l, r)$ of $R$ and words $u$ and $v$ with $w = u l v$ and $w' = u r v$.
nodes.title: One-step rewriting

nodes.summary: For an instance $(R, x, y)$ of the reachability problem, where $R = [(l_1, r_1), \dots, (l_k, r_k)]$ is a list of rewriting rules and $x$, $y$ are words, the letters of the instance form the word $l_1 r_1 l_2 r_2 \cdots l_k r_k \, x \, y$, a list in which a letter may occur several times.
nodes.title: Letters of a rewriting instance

nodes.summary: On an instance $(R, x, y)$, where $R$ is a list of rewriting rules and $x$, $y$ are words, the word problem asks whether $x$ and $y$ are related by the equivalence relation generated by the one-step rewriting relation of $R$, that is, by its reflexive, symmetric and transitive closure.
nodes.title: The word problem of a Thue system

nodes.summary: Let $(R, x, y)$ be an instance of the reachability problem over an alphabet $\alpha$, where $R = [(l_1, r_1), \dots, (l_k, r_k)]$, and write $\#$ for the separator and $\diamond$ for the end marker of the extended alphabet $\mathrm{Sym}(\alpha)$, in which letters of $\alpha$ are read as letters. Let $a_1 \cdots a_m$ be the word $l_1 r_1 l_2 r_2 \cdots l_k r_k \, x \, y$, the letters of the instance. The MPCP…
nodes.title: The MPCP instance of a reachability instance
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
